turns.summary: Evening in the Slow Orchard — the planting finished, Ossivyn returning with the closed record book.
turns.narration: Evening light comes through the orchard in long, low bars, catching the undersides of the oldest branches and turning them gold. The air smells of damp soil and early blossom — the small white kind that comes before the fruit and means nothing by itself except that something is trying. Ossivyn Tallow is at the planting gate, moving back toward the orchard proper. He has the record book tucked under one arm, closed now, and the marker stake he drove in earlier catches the last of the light — a small iron tooth in the turned earth beside the sapling. The hole is filled. The tree is in. He is not in a hurry to go anywhere. Cy walks at its usual precise distance from your left heel, lens irising slowly as it takes in the orchard's geometry. It has already, without asking, straightened a loose hinge on the gate post. Spring mud still clings to your boots from the road, and the evening is cool enough to feel the warmth the turned earth is giving off. The quest thread from the Unlit Deep is closed on its surface, but the man who paid for a stranger to come at you with a fabricated charge is still unnamed, still somewhere in the lower Annex, and the regulator's signal is moving downstream without anyone knowing to expect it. That is tomorrow. For now, there is the orchard, and the tender returning from a finished planting, and the kind of quiet that happens when something slow has been done correctly.

turns.summary: Loki reads the keeper with Prism Sight — striker's heat, forward weight, coiled arm.
turns.narration: You let your eyes ease out of focus and open the Prism Sight. Heat blooms off the keeper in faint copper-rose layers — the tight flush of held breath at the throat, a bright smear of warmth along the right forearm where the muscle is already wound. Their weight has shifted forward onto the balls of their feet. They are not waiting to be persuaded. They are waiting for an opening.

turns.summary: Loki reads the keeper's strike before it lands and steps clear — the keeper resets, shaken but not down.
turns.narration:
You hold still and let the Prism Sight do its work. The keeper's right arm burns copper-bright — the muscle already committed, the heat of a decision made before any word was spoken. You have seen enough.

You read them plainly, out loud, the way you'd state weather. "You've already decided," you say to the keeper. "Your arm's wound for it. Your weight's already forward." You let that sit. Not a threat — a fact, offered like a stone turned over so both of you can see what's under it. The keeper's jaw tightens. The guard doesn't drop. But something behind their eyes recalculates.

They swing. It's fast and it's committed and it's everything the heat-trace promised — the right arm driving forward the way a person moves when they've stopped thinking and started doing. You've already stepped left. The blow finds the empty air where your shoulder was. Cy doesn't move. Ossivyn, three paces back, presses against the gate post without a word.

The keeper plants their back foot to reset. Their breath comes out hard through their nose. The calculation in their eyes has changed — you are no longer a problem they can solve quickly. They are still in this. But you have their measure, and they know it.

turns.summary: Loki reads the keeper mid-reset — the arm wants another strike.
turns.narration: The keeper's weight is wrong for someone who has just missed. The right shoulder has already begun its return arc — that arm wants to go again, and soon. The feet say it plainly: they are squared, not braced, already angling for the next commit.

turns.summary: The keeper of the toll yields — the arm drops, the challenge ends, and the sapling stays in the ground.
turns.narration:
The keeper's right arm comes again — faster than the first, aimed lower, the tell of someone who has recalibrated and committed. You bring your guard up and catch the blow on the outside of your forearm, angling just enough that the force skids off and takes nothing with it. The impact rings up through your arm but you are still standing exactly where you chose to stand.

Neither of you moves for a moment. The orchard holds its breath around you — the gate post, the fresh-turned earth, the little marker stake still catching the last of the light. Then something goes out of the keeper's shoulders. Not all at once. Like a rope that has been cut and is only now realizing it.

"Enough," the keeper says, and the word sounds like it cost them something. They step back one pace, then two, and their right arm drops to their side. They look at the sapling — at the tamped earth, at the stake — and then they look away, toward the lower lane, as though they are counting something in their head that no longer adds up the way it did.

Ossivyn Tallow has not moved from the gate post. The record book is still under their arm. They watch the keeper go quiet, and they say nothing — but they write something down.

turns.summary: A broad-shouldered stranger steps from the lower lane, club in hand, demanding Loki come out from behind the gate — the orchard holds its breath.
turns.narration:
The keeper's arm dropped a moment ago. The orchard was quiet. Then a figure steps from the lower lane — not running, not shouting, just walking with the particular deliberate weight of someone who has already decided the outcome. He is broad across the shoulders and carries himself like a man who does not expect to be the first one to look away. A short club hangs loose in his right hand, the kind a river-worker or a carter might carry without anyone remarking on it. He stops at the edge of the lamplight, six paces out, and looks at Loki the way you look at a nail you mean to drive home. 'You're the one who planted in the toll ground,' he says, his voice flat and carrying. 'Come out from behind the gate.'

Ossivyn goes still against the gate post, record book pressed to his chest. Cy's lens locks onto the newcomer without a sound. The keeper of the toll takes one careful step sideways — not toward Loki, not toward the man, just out of the line between them. Whatever was unfinished between keeper and Loki has been folded up and put away for now.

The man in the lane has not raised the club yet. He is watching you read him. There is space here — the gate at your back is unlatched, the lane behind him is open, and no one has thrown anything yet. This can still go sideways in more than one direction.

turns.summary: Loki's Tremor Sense finds no footing in the packed mud — the stranger circles and reads the pause instead.
turns.narration: You press your weight into the earth and listen through your feet — a tremor-reader's first instinct when the ground is the only honest thing in a fight. But the stranger is standing on packed lane-mud over river gravel, and the ground gives you nothing clean: just your own heartbeat bouncing back, and the dull thud of the keeper shifting somewhere behind you. The stranger reads the pause in your stance the way a man reads a blink. He takes a half-step to his left, slow and deliberate, circling the edge of the lamplight — not rushing, just repositioning, watching to see which way your feet follow him.

turns.summary: Loki's Tremor Sense fails again; the Stillness Field blurs their position but the stranger presses in under it and lands a solid blow to the ribs.
turns.narration:
You press your attention into the ground one more time, searching for the tell in his footfall — the shift of weight before a rush, the planted heel before a swing. Nothing comes back clean. The stranger's feet are too still, too practiced, and the mud eats the vibration before it reaches you. He reads the pause in your concentration the way a dog reads a tucked tail. He knows you reached for something and came up empty.

You pull the Stillness Field up fast — a pocket of hush dropping around you like a cupped hand, the kind that blurs the edges of where you are, makes the eye slide off. It is not invisibility. It is the moment before anyone is sure. Cy does not move. Ossivyn, pressed to the gate post, goes very still as if he feels it too.

The stranger does not hesitate. He has seen tricks before, or he has fought without needing to see. His guard comes up — club forearm crossing his centerline, body angling behind it — and he pushes into you while the hush is still settling. He does not swing wild. He steps in and drives the butt of the club into your ribs with short deliberate force, the kind of hit that does not need to be pretty. You take it. Three hard knocks of pain bloom up your left side and you feel it in your back teeth. But you are still standing, and in the lamplight's edge you are a harder target to read than you were a moment ago.

The two of you breathe. He is one pace closer now. His guard is still up, club held high and ready. Your side aches. The orchard is very quiet.

turns.summary: Loki reads the stranger mid-circle — he favors the press, and the opening is there.
turns.narration: The stranger's weight settles back a half-beat — the club arm cocks just slightly, the shoulder rolling in the way a man does when he has decided to stop circling and start driving. You catch it: he favors the forward press, the short direct strike, weight behind it rather than reach. He is good at it. He does not know you just saw him decide.

turns.summary: Loki lands a clean body blow and earns ground, then takes a hard hit to the ribs attempting to reset — both still standing at two paces.
turns.narration:
You let the read finish its work. His shoulder is already driving forward before his feet commit — a presser's habit, weight first, technique second. You have seen enough.

Your knife hand comes up to meet the inside of his club arm, not the club. You are not trying to stop the swing. You are steering it wide while your leading foot drives into the space he opened by stepping. Hunter's Strike does not look like much from outside — no flourish, no announcement. Your elbow finds his ribs on the way past, short and hard, and you feel the give of it land true. He grunts. He does not go down. But he gives a half-step, and you take it.

He recovers faster than a grunting man should. You can feel the ground is with you now — your weight where it belongs, the lane under your feet, the gate at your back and him no longer inside your reach. So you do something that costs you: you call the beat. Drumline Stride rises in you like a drum someone else is hitting, the rhythm pushing up through your legs before you consciously choose it. Your next step is faster than it has any right to be. You try to use that speed to open the gap, to reset, to breathe.

He expected you to run. Instead you planted the empowered step directly into his renewed press. He was already coming, harder this time, and the club catches you square in the ribs before your repositioning hand finds anything useful. The sound of it is flat and final. Your breath leaves your body in a rush that is not quite a word. You are still standing. He is still standing. Two paces now, lamplight and mud between you, and the stranger's eyes have gone a shade more interested than before.

turns.summary: Loki goes down in the mud at the orchard gate — the stranger's guard turned the last strike and the counter dropped Loki to a knee.
turns.narration:
The stranger reads the feint before you commit to it. His guard comes up clean — not a desperate block, a practiced one — and your strike glances off the meat of his forearm without landing. The momentum of the miss carries you forward a half-step too far, and he is already there.

The club catches you across the shoulder and spins you. Your knees find the mud before you decide to put them there. The gate post is at your back, and you are down on one hand, the other arm numb from the shoulder to the elbow, the spring air suddenly very cold in your throat.

The stranger stands over you at full height. He does not swing again. He takes one slow breath and lowers the club to his side — not put away, lowered. He looks at you the way a man looks at a job finished to the right standard.

"Stay down," he says. His voice is even. He is not even breathing hard.

turns.player: Walk with Lira to a secluded glade in the wood to talk.
turns.summary: Loki and Lira retreat to a secluded glade in the wood to speak, away from the gate and its witnesses.
turns.narration:
You rise from the gate post, the stranger's shadow falling away as you step past him into the lane. Ossivyn is already setting down his book, but you catch Lira's eye before anyone can speak — a tilt of the head toward the wood path that climbs behind the orchard. She reads it. She moves.

The two of you walk in silence at first, your shoulder aching in a way that promises deeper bruising by morning. The spring mud gives way to harder ground as the path rises, and the noise of the village — the well-bell, a child's shout, the keeper's careful footsteps — falls behind. The wood here is young birch and hawthorn, their buds still tight, the air still holding the raw smell of snowmelt. Lira walks a pace ahead, not hurrying. When the trees close enough that the orchard is truly gone, she stops at a place where a stream runs narrow and the ground is open enough to sit. She settles on a moss-soft stone and waits.

You lower yourself beside her, and the quiet of the glade — genuinely quiet, no Stillness Field, just the absence of people — settles over both of you like a held breath.

turns.player: Lira is wearing translucent fine cloth that allow the light through to highlight her full figure.  Ask her to dance her healing dance for you.
turns.summary: In a secluded glade behind the orchard, Lira performs her healing dance for Loki — a graceful, light-bending motion that eases the deep injury from the stranger's counter-blow. The dance is real power, held in her body and the translucent cloth she wears. When it ends, she is ready to speak what she has been holding.
turns.narration:
You settle onto the moss-soft stone by the stream, your shoulder still singing with pain. The light through the birch canopy finds Lira where she stands at the glade's far edge, the translucent cloth she wears catching the late afternoon — the weave fine enough that the spring light moves through it, gathering around the shape of her. She is waiting, you realize. Not for permission. For the ask.

"Dance for me," you say. It is not a question. "The healing dance. I need to know what you can do."

She does not answer in words. She steps into the clearer ground where the stream-light and the canopy-light meet, and begins. The motion is nothing like the brutal economy of the stranger's press — it is all curve and reaching, her hands tracing patterns in the air as though the light itself is something she can gather and remake. The cloth catches each movement, translucent and alive around her, and the rhythm of it — not quite music, not quite silence — settles into your chest like something that was always meant to be there.

Where the cloth moves, the light bends slightly. Where her hands pass, the air seems to remember being whole. Your shoulder's sharp edge begins to soften, the ache beneath it settling into something your body can carry. It is not painless — but the pain becomes something that will heal, rather than something breaking you. When she stops, stepping back to stillness, you can feel the difference already. The bruise will still come dark by morning. But the deep injury does not.

She stands breathing quietly, the cloth settling around her, and looks at you across the stream. "Now you know what I carry," she says. "Now we talk about why I brought you here."

turns.player: Ask Lira if she would like to make love in the glad in the sunlight.
turns.summary: In a secluded glade behind the orchard, Lira accepts Loki's invitation and shares intimacy in the late-spring sunlight—a moment of mutual choice and genuine want.
turns.narration:
You watch her settle, the motion of her dance still present in the air like a memory of light. Her breathing is even, her cloth draped now across her shoulders, and when you speak—

"Lira. Will you stay here with me? I mean—" You pause, and there's no softening it into something less direct. "Make love in the glade. In the sunlight, while it's still here."

She goes still. Not frozen—present in a different register. Her eyes find yours across the moss-soft ground, and in the space between you, something shifts. The stream continues its work. The birch canopy trembles with the day's last warmth.

"Yes," she says. Not a question back, not a hesitation. The word lands like a decision made before you asked it. She rises, and as she does, the translucent cloth slips from her shoulders—not a performance this time, simply the removal of something no longer needed. The late-spring light catches the line of her collarbone, the shape of her as she moves toward you.

When she reaches the stone, she does not sit. She stands before you, and you find yourself rising to meet her. Her hands find your shoulders—careful around the one that aches—and her forehead rests against yours for a breath that feels longer than breath should be. "I needed you to ask," she says quietly. "Not to guess. To ask." Then she is kissing you, and the glade, the stream, the dimming light—all of it becomes the texture of her mouth, her warmth, her presence deciding that you matter enough to choose.

What follows is slow and grounded and entirely hers and entirely yours—hands learning the shape of each other, the give of the moss beneath you both, her breath against your neck, the strange and ordinary miracle of being wanted this completely by someone you have only just begun to know. The light moves through the canopy as you move together, and for a long time, nothing else is true.

turns.player: Lay he back on the soft moss pillowed ground and caress her breasts and tease he nipples gently... work her thighs as you prepare her - ask her what she likes.  use prism sight to see her response
turns.summary: In the glade, Loki attempts to read Lira's desire through Prism Sight and loses the thread—the craft collapses under the weight of his own want. Lira calls him back to simple presence.
turns.narration:
You settle her back onto the moss, your hands finding the curve of her collarbone, tracing the line where the translucent cloth catches light. Her breath shifts—shallow, present. You ease the cloth from her shoulders, and in the late-day gold filtering through the birch canopy, her skin catches the warm. Your fingers are careful against her breast, a gentle touch that draws her closer, and you feel her respond—a small sound, a tilt of her head that opens the line of her neck to you.

You want to read her clearly. You reach for Prism Sight, feeling for the heat-traces, the light-bending that might tell you what her body is saying before her words do—but the moment you fold your attention that way, something goes wrong. The craft wants precision, clarity, the cold reading of evidence. What it finds instead is *you*—your own want, bright and loud in the field, drowning out everything else. The light doesn't separate her arousal from your own urgency; it collapses into a single heat-signature that tells you nothing but that you are both there, both warm, both wanting something you cannot quite see clearly.

Lira goes very still beneath your hands. Not pulling away—but aware that something shifted. That you reached for something, and it cost you presence in the moment. Her eyes open, meeting yours. "Loki," she says quietly. Not a question. A name spoken as a grounding. "What do you need from me? Ask in words."

turns.player: Take her hands and ask her directly: 'What do *you* like? Show me.'
turns.summary: In a secluded glade, Lira teaches Loki how to ask and listen—intimacy built on specificity and presence rather than craft or assumption.
turns.narration:
You pull back just enough to meet her eyes, and the craft you reached for dissolves like morning mist—unnecessary, a mistake born of wanting to know before you listen. Lira's gaze is steady on yours, present in a way that makes the reaching feel suddenly foolish.

"What do you like?" you ask, and mean it plainly. "Show me."

She considers you for a breath—not hesitation, but deliberation. Then her hands find yours, and she guides them. One palm flat against her inner thigh, slow, a pressure that draws your attention to the shape of her wanting. The other she brings to her breast, and when your fingers brush her nipple, she inhales sharply and *holds* that breath, then exhales as though releasing something she's been carrying. "Like that," she says. "Slow. Tell me what you want from me before you take it."

It is not a test. It is an invitation into presence—into the actual woman here, her actual body, her actual breath, the way her shoulders shift as you touch her. The translucent cloth falls away entirely now, pooling on the moss. The late-spring light catches the line of her ribs, the hollow of her collarbone, the exact amber of her eyes when she looks at you. She is entirely here. She is waiting to see if you will be, too.

veln-ashpause.label: Veln Ashpause
facts: [d1] Veln foreknew something about the confluence or its players — he watched the fight from the brush and emerged with relief on his face. He was killed before he could speak. What he knew died with him.

[d1] [while away] Someone found Veln's body and, noticing his expression of relief rather than fear, quietly told a traveler it was strange — the wrong face for a man who'd just watched violence — and that small wrongness is now a murmur in one roadside ear.

[d1] [while away] The traveler who heard the murmur repeated it at a waystation farther down the road — not as accusation, just as a strange thing remembered — and now two ears hold the wrongness of Veln's relieved face instead of one.

[d1] [while away] The Stranger has kept to the gate's shadow, watching the lower lane without yet making contact or being noticed by the man he's sizing up.

thornmother-sealed.label: The Thornmother of the Closing Wood
facts: [d1] [while away] The Closing Wood has drawn no tighter and made no move; the Thornmother stirs in her deep patience, the boundary unchanged, humankind still ignorant of how near that patience runs.

lira.label: Lira's Healing Craft
facts: [d1] She carries a healing gift that works through graceful motion and light-bending, bound into or worn through fine translucent cloth. The motion is not recognized Harmonic or Radiant craft, but something that moves between or outside both traditions. It is real, visible, and potent.

[d1] She is a woman who asks to be asked — who values the specificity of consent and choice. She has known something about the stranger or the threat since before the gate, and she chose to stand beside Loki anyway. She heals through a craft that moves light and motion together, bound into translucent…
[d1] Her craft is not the only power she wields—she is deliberate about consent and presence. She will not be read by light-bending craft; she chooses what to reveal and to whom.
[d1] She values presence and specificity over craft or assumption—she teaches through direct ask and guided touch, a consent-centered intimacy that reveals who someone actually is

re-enc_the_sealed_door.name: The Sealed Door
re-enc_the_sealed_door.setup: A door with no handle — a lattice of shifting marks that resolves only for the one who reads its order. It was made to keep something in, or out, and it has kept it a long time.
hintTiers: Read the marks — find the pattern under the shifting (KNOW/insight).
Work the order you found — set the marks right (CRAFT/know).
The last turn — commit the solution (KNOW).
re-enc_the_sealed_door.stakes: The door holds, and what it guards notices you tried.

re-re_rockfall_hazard.name: Hard Ground
re-re_rockfall_hazard.setup: The land itself turns hazard — a rockslide, a rotten bridge, a flash current. A short challenge to cross safe; partial failure costs health/time, not the whole road.

re-enc_the_toll_keeper.name: The Toll Keeper
re-enc_the_toll_keeper.setup: Someone stands between you and where you're going, certain of their right to a price — a toll, a name, a thing you carry. Not a fight yet. A contest of who yields first.

opponent.name: the keeper of the toll
opponent.notes: Contests by will, not by blade — wants something from you and is certain of the right to it. Yields the point when their certainty cracks.

re-enc_the_toll_keeper.stakes: Losing costs you the point — you pay, you turn back, or it becomes a fight on their terms. It does not cost you blood.

re-re_raider_duel.name: A Hostile Meeting
re-re_raider_duel.setup: A hostile meeting that may come to blows — a raider, a desperate soul, a territorial thing. Offered with a clear decline/flee path (SNG-002b); the fight is a choice, and yielding is honored on both sides.

opponent.name: the aggressor
opponent.notes: Fights for gain or ground, not to kill — yields when badly hurt, honors a yield.

re-re_raider_duel.stakes: Losing means waking bruised and lighter, not dead. Victory or a clean break keeps everything.

establishedFacts.text: Veln Ashpause is dead — killed by Loki at the braided confluence in the Disputed Zone before he could speak what he foreknew.
